message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Operating System** | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (Focal) |
| **GPU** | NVIDIA RTX A6000 |
| **Machine type** | `n1-standard-8` (8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – you can adjust as needed) |
| **Zone** | `us-central1-a` (or any zone that supports RTX A6000) |
| **Project ID** | `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` (replace with your actual GCP project ID) |
| **Service account** | `YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com` (must have Compute Admin & Service Account User roles) |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does **not** use “EC2”; that’s Amazon Web Services. In GCP the equivalent is Compute Engine.*  
> *Make sure the Compute Engine API is enabled in your project and that you have the necessary IAM permissions.*

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣ Set variables
PROJECT="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
SERVICE_ACCOUNT="YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@${PROJECT}.iam.gserviceaccount.com"

# 2️⃣ Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create ${INSTANCE_NAME} \
  --project=${PROJECT} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=${MACHINE_TYPE} \
  --image-family=${IMAGE_FAMILY} \
  --image-project=${IMAGE_PROJECT} \
  --accelerator=type=${GPU_TYPE},count=${GPU_COUNT} \
  --service-account=${SERVICE_ACCOUNT} \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### Optional: Startup Script (`startup.sh`)

If you want to install NVIDIA drivers and CUDA automatically:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470

# Install CUDA Toolkit (optional)
wget https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/cuda-ubuntu2004.pin
mv cuda-ubuntu2004.pin /etc/apt/preferences.d/cuda-repository-pin-600
add-apt-repository "deb http://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/ /"
apt-key adv --fetch-keys https://developer.download.nvidia.com/compute/cuda/repos/ubuntu2004/x86_64/7fa2af80.pub
apt-get update
apt-get install -y cuda

# Reboot to load drivers
reboot
```

> **Tip:** If you prefer not to reboot automatically, remove the `reboot` line and manually restart the instance after the script finishes.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a custom application), here’s the exact JSON payload you would POST to:

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT@YOUR_PROJECT_ID.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-470\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### REST API Call Example (curl)

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

> Replace `instance.json` with the path to a file containing the JSON above.

---

## 3. Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | Service account with `roles/compute.admin` & `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` |
| ✅ | Zone supports RTX A6000 (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.) |
| ✅ | GPU quota available (request if needed) |
| ✅ | Proper firewall rules (HTTP/HTTPS) if you plan to expose services |

---

### Final Thoughts

- **GPU Quotas**: RTX A6000 is a high‑end GPU; you’ll likely need to request a quota increase if you haven’t already.
- **Driver Version**: The example installs NVIDIA driver 470. Adjust if you need a newer version.
- **CUDA**: If you’re doing GPU‑accelerated workloads, install the matching CUDA toolkit (the script above pulls the latest for Ubuntu 20.04).

Happy computing! 🚀
